$comment: Files that still mention `inngest` or `domains/desk` (any case) after `init-app --desk no`, and why each stays. tools/init-app/check-variants.mjs (pnpm verify:scaffold) fails on a hit that is not here and on an entry that no longer matches. `match` is always one of the two bare search strings. The search skips what the rename walker skips (tools/init-app/, docs/superpowers/).

entries.reason: The production guard refuses INNGEST_DEV in every product: a deployment that sets it by mistake must not boot, Desk or not.
isInngestDevMode(), which the production guard in configuration.ts calls.
The spec of the INNGEST_DEV production guard, which stays.
Documents the production checks, the INNGEST_DEV refusal among them.
A comment saying where a feature registers its own prompts; the prompting module and the DESK_MEMORY_EXTRACT key stay (ADR "Optional features: Desk is opt-in at scaffold time").
A decision record: it lists the provider routes as decided, the Inngest serve handler among them. Records are not edited per product.
A decision record: it says why a timer no longer needs a workflow engine, which is what made Desk optional.
The decision record for Desk opt-in. It stays in every product, so a product without Desk knows what was removed and how to add it back.
The decision record for Desk opt-in names the Desk folder the seam guards.

A decision record: it says state stays in Postgres while an engine only orchestrates, naming the engine Desk runs on as the case. It holds in a product without Desk, which is why removing Desk loses no state.
The pnpm verify:scaffold gate text names the residue search strings.
The pnpm verify:scaffold gate text names the residue search strings.
The architecture spec that keeps the AI domain from importing Desk names the Desk folder it guards. It must stay in a product without Desk, so a later change cannot make AI depend on Desk again.

FEATURE_FOLDERS names the Desk folder: the skills guard fails on a requires: desk skill, reference or hotspot file when that folder is absent, which is how a product without Desk catches a returning Desk file.
reservedNames lists <name>-inngest, the container name init-app renames, so no skill or agent name may start with it. Every product keeps the list, Desk or not.
Counts the desk feature key as covered when the Desk folder does not exist, so the spec passes in a product scaffolded without Desk (design item 17).
